title: Avril TESS discovery target queue v0.2

catalog.model_applicability: All 1,000 bundled targets were in the frozen stellar-model training domain.

interpretation.plain_language: These scores choose which stars are worth searching first. They are not the probability that a star has a planet and are not evidence of a transit.
interpretation.catalog_count_prior: The ordinal outputs estimate yield in a frozen, high-reliability Kepler DR25 catalog under explicit period, radius, S/N and transit-count cuts. They are lower-bound catalog-yield priors, not the unknown true number of planets.
interpretation.gap_score: The gap and lane scores combine the frozen stellar prior with transparent opportunity features such as TESS coverage, revisit baseline, detectability proxies and known-system status. They are ranking heuristics, not calibrated probabilities.
interpretation.required_next_step: A target becomes scientifically interesting only after Avril finds repeatable light-curve evidence and it passes catalog deduplication, pixel localization, neighbour checks and physical vetting.

model_profiles.frozen_candidate: Default ordinal catalog-yield prior trained on the frozen high-reliability DR25 candidate definition.
model_profiles.confirmed_clean: More conservative ordinal lower-bound profile that additionally requires the DR25 archive disposition CONFIRMED.
model_profiles.occurrence_grid: Completeness-corrected period-radius occurrence-grid baseline using stellar CDPP, MES thresholds, data span, duty cycle, transit geometry and the DR25 injection-recovery curve.

development_rank_blend.status: Development choice from out-of-fold Kepler predictions; it is not a fresh TESS blind-test result.

validation.split: Five-fold star-level cross-validation using kepid modulo 5; all planets around one star stay in one fold.

quick_repeat.purpose: Prioritize targets where repeated evidence should be relatively quick to obtain.
quick_repeat.recipe: Run the standard multi-detrending search, BLS and TLS; retain every independent event and prefer signals repeated across sectors or years.

known_host_residual.purpose: Search residual light curves of systems already known to host planets.
known_host_residual.recipe: Fit and mask every known ephemeris first; then run BLS, TLS and event-first searches on the residual light curve, retaining more than the highest peak.

long_baseline_event.purpose: Look for long-period single- and double-transit events across mission eras.
long_baseline_event.recipe: Search sector-by-sector for individual transit-like events; match depth and duration across epochs, enumerate period aliases, and reject aliases with missing predicted events.

blind_control.purpose: Retain an exploration/control arm for measuring real enrichment without self-confirming the ranking.
blind_control.recipe: Run the same full standard search without using the framework score when interpreting the result; keep this arm for an unbiased yield comparison.

scientific_caveats: Kepler-to-TESS target selection, bandpass, baseline and noise differences create domain shift.
TESS detectability in this pre-download queue is an approximation; it is not an injection-recovery calibration of Avril.
The occurrence grid does not yet reproduce clustered multi-planet architectures or conditional coplanarity.
Known-record counts and sector coverage are frozen to the queue build snapshot and can become stale.
The blind-control lane must remain in yield comparisons.
